notes: Claims stated over Mathlib's definitions. Mathlib is pinned by commit and built from source with the same toolchain; see reference/mathlib_pin.json. Mathlib's definitions are in the trusted set, so they enter each claim's freeze: a change in Mathlib's Nat.Prime breaks the attestation.

claims.text: There are arbitrarily large prime numbers: for every natural number n there is a prime p with n <= p (Euclid's theorem).

review.note: Stated with Mathlib's Nat.Prime, whose definition the reviewer read (Irreducible in the monoid of naturals, equivalently 2 <= p with no proper divisor). 'Arbitrarily large' is rendered as a forall-exists with n <= p, which is the standard reading of the infinitude of primes; n < p would also be correct and is implied, since p is prime and so p >= 2.
